The only reasonable way is to build the right culture, something we need to be finding consensus on and doing right now. If a proper culture is built, as time passes the older users will pass this to newer users and it'll evolve as these things do. For example, the freedom to speak and mod vigilance are a current core part of voat culture. These things need to continue to be defined so proper boundaries can be set, making it easier to identify, say, outright censorship vs a mod just being aggressive but not overstepping bounds. The latter can happen without a mod necessarily "power tripping" and so on. Remember that mods are human users too.

Can we have a mechanism to vote out mods perhaps?

This has been brought up several times. The consensus was that this would create a very hostile, witch-hunt like environment any time someone disagreed with a mod decision and is therefore not desirable.

The correct way to deal with mods acting out of line is to create a new sub and abandon the sub they moderate. Note that, even if a mod is active on the site, if they don't interact with their sub at least once every 30 days it is considered abandoned by them and is liable to be transferred via /v/subverserequest.

Problem with creating another subverse is, for one, how many members will you retain? You'll be smaller than they are from the start, and you quite possibly would be unable to advertise your new subverse in that one, because it would be deleted. It's okay to post in /v/newsubverses now, but if and when the site grows, that might not be much good, because it would be lost in a little sea of new subverses.

There's never a clean break.

Oh, I never said it would be simple to switch subverses, but this is the recourse. Note that this entire premise is predicated on many people agreeing that this mod is a shithead, which implies there would be a userbase for another sub on the same topic. If the plurality of the sub doesn't want to use the replacement sub then perhaps it's appropriate to consider how bad our bad mod actually is.

The only reasonable way is to build the right culture, something we need to be finding consensus on and doing right now.
